title: DATA 201 Week 3 Session 1
text:
Attributes

What is an attribute?

Qualities and characteristics that describe a data object or instance
Example: Company surveying their employee’s happiness
Data object:  Employee 
Attributes: job position, working-hours satisifaction, team satisfaction

title: DATA 201 Week 3 Session 1
text:
Levels of measurement

Nominal
Ordinal
Interval
Ratio

title: DATA 201 Week 3 Session 1
text:
Nominal

Labels that have no natural order; order is interchangeable
Gender: female, male
Eye colour: brown, green, blue
Place you live: city, suburbs, rural
Languages that you speak: English, French, Spanish
If there are only two categories, we can say that it is binary/dichotomous

yes/no

title: DATA 201 Week 3 Session 1
text:
Ordinal

labels that have a natural/or meaningful order
Very unsatisfied, unsatisfied, neutral, satisfied, very satisfied

satisfied is better than unsatisfied

School grades: A is better than B and B is better than C
Frequency of watching TV

1 = daily
2 = several times a week
3 = several times a month
4 = never

title: DATA 201 Week 3 Session 1
text:
Ratio

Ratio scale has equal intervals
Has a meaningful zero

0 grams means something has no mass

Comparisons are meaningful

100 cm is twice as long as 50 cm
5kgs is half as heavy as 10 kgs

title: DATA 201 Week 3 Session 1
text:
Interval

Also has equal intervals, but no meaningful zero
Difference between 10°C and 20°C is the same size as 20°C and 30°C

BUT 20°C is not twice as hot as 10°C
0°C is not an absolute/meaningful zero

Kelvins has an absolute zero, so it would be ratio
